question: What is the shining surface of the Sun called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**photosphere**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **photosphere** is the shining surface of the Sun that we can observe from Earth.
 
• The photosphere is the lowest visible layer of the Sun's atmosphere, and it is where most of the Sun's light is emitted.
 
• The temperature of the photosphere is approximately **5,500 degrees Celsius** (5,773 Kelvin).
 
• Features such as **sunspots**, which are cooler regions, can be observed on the photosphere.
 
• The photosphere is crucial for solar observations and helps scientists study the Sun's structure and behavior.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Sun** is composed of several layers, including the core, radiative zone, convective zone, photosphere, chromosphere, and corona.
 
• The **chromosphere** is the layer above the photosphere and can be seen during solar eclipses as a reddish glow.
 
• The **corona** is the outermost layer of the Sun's atmosphere, extending millions of kilometers into space and visible during total solar eclipses.
 
• The Sun's energy is produced in its core through the process of **nuclear fusion**.
 
• The study of the Sun and its various layers is known as **heliophysics**.
